claims.text: After entering Beleriand, Ulfast along with his father and his brothers joined the service of Caranthir.
claims.cite: J.R.R. Tolkien, Christopher Tolkien (ed.), The Silmarillion, "Quenta Silmarillion: Of the Ruin of Beleriand and the Fall of Fingolfin"

claims.text: Ultimately though, his father Ulfang's purpose from the beginning was to eventually betray the Elves, which he and his brothers ultimately did in the Battle of Unnumbered Tears, under the leadership of Uldor the Accursed - they turned against their allies, attacking them in the rear. Their betrayal proved crucial in the fight against Morgoth's forces, though, and Morgoth was victorious.
claims.cite: J.R.R. Tolkien, Christopher Tolkien (ed.), The War of the Jewels, "Part One. The Grey Annals": §174, pp. 60-1, footnote; J.R.R. Tolkien, Christopher Tolkien (ed.), The Silmarillion, "Quenta Silmarillion: Of the Fifth Battle: Nirnaeth Arnoediad"

claims.text: However, Ulfast, as well as his brother Ulwarth were killed by the sons of Bór, who remained loyal to the sons of Fëanor during the battle - while Ulfast's brother Uldor was slain by Maglor.
claims.cite: J.R.R. Tolkien, Christopher Tolkien (ed.), The Silmarillion, "Quenta Silmarillion: Of the Fifth Battle: Nirnaeth Arnoediad"

claims.text: According to an earlier version of the legendarium, instead of being killed by the sons of Bór, both Ulfast and his brother Ulwar survived the Battle of Unnumbered Tears - in fact, they were the ones that slew Bor and his sons in battle.
claims.cite: J.R.R. Tolkien, Christopher Tolkien (ed.), The Lost Road and Other Writings, "Part Two: Valinor and Middle-earth before The Lord of the Rings, III. The Later Annals of Beleriand", entry 272, p. 137
claims.section: section == Other versions of the legendarium == > Earlier versions of the Nirnaeth

claims.text: Afterwards, the folk of Ulfast and Ulwar brutally oppressed the remaining native folk of Hádor who were already living there before their arrival.
claims.cite: J.R.R. Tolkien, Christopher Tolkien (ed.), The Lost Road and Other Writings, "Part Two: Valinor and Middle-earth before The Lord of the Rings, III. The Later Annals of Beleriand", entry 273, p. 138
claims.section: section == Other versions of the legendarium == > Earlier versions of the Nirnaeth

claims.text: In the appendix of The Lost Road and Other Writings in The Genealogies (dating from the early 1930s), it is stated that Ulfast was born in the year 128.
claims.cite: J.R.R. Tolkien, Christopher Tolkien (ed.), The Lost Road and Other Writings, "Appendix: I. The Genealogies", p. 403
claims.section: section == Other versions of the legendarium == > Ulfast's year of birth

claims.text: When comparing the above date with its associated text The Earliest Annals of Beleriand, Ulfast was born 35 years before the Swarthy Men entered Beleriand in the year 163.
claims.cite: J.R.R. Tolkien, Christopher Tolkien (ed.), The Shaping of Middle-earth, "VII. The Earliest Annals of Beleriand: [The first version of The Earliest Annals of Beleriand (Text AB I)]", entry year 163, p. 300
claims.section: section == Other versions of the legendarium == > Ulfast's year of birth

claims.text: Also, the dates found in The Earliest Annals of Beleriand were by and large moved 300 years into the future in The Grey Annals (c. early 1950s), such that, for example, an event happening in the year 195 in The Earliest Annals now happened in the year .
claims.cite: J.R.R. Tolkien, Christopher Tolkien (ed.), The Shaping of Middle-earth, "VII. The Earliest Annals of Beleriand: Commentary on the Annals of Beleriand (text AB I)", Annals 155 to 157, pp. 319-20
claims.section: section == Other versions of the legendarium == > Ulfast's year of birth
